title: "CausalPhylo: causal identification of drug-resistance drivers in HIV-1 phylodynamics"
subtitle: "Applying SAWA to distinguish selection from confounding in East African resistance surveillance"
author:
  - name: Kelyn Njeri
    orcid: 0000-0000-0000-0000  # replace when issued
    email: kelyn@neoforge.io

      - name: NeoForge Labs, Nairobi, Kenya
abstract: |
  Which observed shifts in HIV-1 drug-resistance frequency are caused by
  which interventions — DTG rollout, ART regimen changes, adherence
  programs — versus explained by sampling bias, subtype confounding,
  and unobserved treatment history? We apply the DoWhy causal-inference
  framework to Stanford HIVdb Sierra calls from the SAWA platform's
  East African cohort (KE, UG, TZ, RW, BI, ET; ~25 000 sequences,
  1994–2024) via a domain DAG that makes the confounders explicit:
  latent treatment history mediated through drug pressure, latent
  subtype-polymorphism context, and direct subtype effects on Sierra
  rules. For each mutation → resistance edge we report identified
  effect estimates with bootstrap confidence intervals plus three
  refutations (placebo, random common cause, subset). We contrast
  effect estimates that survive refutation with those that don't, and
  demonstrate that some strong associations (e.g., of
  polymorphism-adjacent positions) collapse under placebo challenge —
  a result that observational surveillance treating these positions as
  causal drivers cannot see.

# Introduction

<!--
The observational-surveillance problem: correlations between mutations
and resistance labels can be driven by unobserved treatment history,
subtype-specific polymorphism, and sampling. Motivate why causal
identification matters for a public-health platform.
-->

# Methods

## Data — SAWA v0.1.0

We use the frozen data vintage from SAWA release `v0.1.0-sawa` (Zenodo
DOI `10.xxxx/xxxxxxx`), comprising `${N_SEQUENCES}` HIV-1 *pol*
sequences from `${N_COUNTRIES}` East African countries pulled from
LANL and GenBank between `${YEAR_MIN}` and `${YEAR_MAX}`.

## Domain DAG

![Drug-resistance domain DAG. Observed nodes (mutation features, subtype,
country, collection year) are drawn as solid boxes; latent confounders
(treatment history, drug pressure, polymorphism context) as
dashed.](figures/fig01_dr_dag.pdf){#fig-dr-dag}

The DAG (@fig-dr-dag) is committed as `causal/dag.py::DRDag` and
serialized via `to_dowhy_gml()`. Minimum backdoor adjustment for each
mutation is `{subtype, country, collection_year}`, derived
programmatically from the DAG structure — no manual per-mutation
adjustment lists.

## Identification and estimation

For each mutation → resistance edge we identify the backdoor
estimand via DoWhy `identify_effect`, then estimate under a logistic
regression outcome model with bootstrap 95 % percentile intervals
(200 resamples). We stratify by subtype as a lightweight interaction
proxy (@sec-interaction).

## Refutation

Three refuters per estimate:
1. **Placebo treatment** — replace the treatment with a random
   assignment; the effect should collapse near zero.
2. **Random common cause** — inject a random confounder; the effect
   should be robust.
3. **Subset validity** — re-estimate on a random 80 % subset; the
   effect should be stable.

A refuter is scored PASSES / FAILS / INCONCLUSIVE based on the ratio
of new-to-original estimate (tolerance ±20 %). Effects that fail ≥ 2/3
refuters are flagged as candidate spurious associations.

## Feature pruning

Rule-based post-hoc pruning (`causal/pruning.py`) drops mutations whose
CI spans zero with small effect magnitude OR that fail refutation
across scopes. `keep-wins-across-scopes` policy prevents a mutation
from being dropped globally when it's causally identified in *any*
data slice.

# Results

## Data adapter and preprocessing

The `causal/data_prep.py` adapter builds per-drug-class analytical
frames from SAWA's Paper 1 outputs. Mutation binary features are
extracted from Sierra's per-drug mutation lists (`M184V` → `RT_184_V`);
covariates are joined from the curated silver Parquet. See
[`data_prep.py`](https://github.com/Neoforge-Labs/SAWA/blob/main/causal/data_prep.py)
for the exact mapping.
